headline: Software Leads, Chips Lag as PTC Steals the Monday Spotlight
body_html:
Monday's session is shaping up as a tale of two ends of the technology spectrum. Software sits atop the sector leaderboard, up 1.18%, while Semiconductors and Homebuilders are the clear laggards, off 1.10% and 1.16% respectively. Across the 544-stock universe tracked by this desk, 296 names are advancing against 243 in the red, a modestly positive tilt that reflects caution rather than conviction.

The dominant story of the morning is PTC Inc., the industrial-software firm surging 34.72% — a move that stands well clear of every other name on the tape. Freight broker RXO Inc. is also commanding attention, up 22.33%, though that sharp gain is clouded by a near-mirror-image collapse in rival C.H. Robinson, which has shed 11.82% and sits at the foot of the decline table. Storage names Western Digital and Seagate Technology are quietly adding 6.26% and 5.33%, providing support beneath Software's leadership.

Heading into the close, traders will be watching whether the chip sector can arrest its slide — United Microelectronics is down 10.73% and Credo Technology off 4.20%, keeping the broader semiconductor group under pressure. Homebuilder Lennar's 3.50% drop is another thread worth monitoring as Tuesday's session approaches.

briefs.headline: PTC's Extraordinary Leap Anchors Software's Monday Surge
briefs.body: PTC Inc. has rocketed 34.72% through Monday's midday hours, single-handedly pulling the Software-Industrial corner of the market into the conversation. Fellow software name Bentley Systems is adding a comparatively measured 7.59%, reinforcing the sector's lead on the day. No other group comes close to matching Software's 1.18% aggregate gain.

briefs.headline: Freight Sector Tells Two Very Different Stories
briefs.body: RXO Inc. is soaring 22.33%, one of the session's most striking moves outside of PTC, while logistics rival C.H. Robinson has tumbled 11.82% — the steepest percentage decline across the entire tracked universe. The divergence suggests company-specific catalysts rather than a broad freight-market trend are driving both moves simultaneously.

briefs.headline: Chip Stocks Under Sustained Pressure at Midday
briefs.body: Semiconductors are the worst-performing major sector at negative 1.10%, with United Microelectronics down 10.73% and Credo Technology off 4.20% leading the retreat. Skyworks Solutions is also softer, falling 3.47%. The weakness spans foundry, connectivity, and RF sub-segments, pointing to broad rather than isolated selling pressure in the group.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Slip as Lennar Weighs on the Group
briefs.body: The Homebuilders sector is off 1.16% midday, making it the joint-weakest corner of the market alongside Semiconductors. Lennar is contributing meaningfully to that pain with a 3.50% decline. With interest-rate sentiment remaining unsettled, analysts will be watching whether buyers step in before the bell or leave the sector to close near its lows.

briefs.headline: Storage Stocks Offer a Quiet Bright Spot in Tech
briefs.body: While chip designers struggle, storage hardware names are catching a bid. Western Digital has climbed 6.26% and Seagate Technology is up 5.33%, providing one of the session's more consistent pockets of tech-related strength. The gains suggest the market may be drawing a distinction between storage fundamentals and the broader semiconductor supply-chain concerns weighing on the sector.

briefs.headline: Fire Reported Near Saudi Energy Facility Keeps Energy Names Firm
briefs.body: Reports of fire and smoke visible near an Aramco facility in Riyadh are circulating midday, injecting a fresh geopolitical note into commodity markets. Energy is among Monday's stronger sectors, up 0.98%. Traders will be monitoring any official statements from Saudi authorities, as supply-disruption concerns could extend Energy's relative outperformance into Tuesday's open.
